description: invite.rs lines 182-189: invite code = format\!("{:012x}", SystemTime::now().as_nanos() & 0xffff_ffff_ffff). This is a predictable 48-bit value seeded from nanosecond wall-clock time. An attacker who knows the approximate invite creation time can enumerate the code space. The comment acknowledges this is 'sufficient for MemoryBackend/test context' but the function ships as library code with no override mechanism — production callers get the same predictable implementation. Fix: accept an optional code parameter from the backend, or document a required hook; default generation must use a CSPRNG (e.g. getrandom). Acceptance: invite code generation uses cryptographically random bytes for production callers.
title: SpaceInvite code is nanosecond-timestamp-seeded, not cryptographically random
